spec.description: Live broadcasts, most watched first, filtered by broadcaster, category or language. A broadcaster who is not live is simply absent from the answer. Viewers come and go while a walk is in flight, so a stream can be seen twice or missed across pages.

request.title: GetStreamsRequest
request.description: Which live broadcasts, and which page of them.

user_id.description: Only these broadcasters, by user id. Sent as repeated `user_id` query parameters; at most 100.

user_login.description: Only these broadcasters, by login name, such as `twitchdev`. Sent as repeated `user_login` query parameters; at most 100.

game_id.description: Only broadcasts of these categories, by category id. Sent as repeated `game_id` query parameters; at most 100.

type.description: The type of broadcast to return. Defaults to `all`.

language.description: Only broadcasts in these languages, as ISO 639-1 two-letter codes, or `other` for a language Twitch does not list. Sent as repeated `language` query parameters; at most 100.

first.description: Rows per page. Range [1, 100]; defaults to 20.

after.description: Cursor for the next page, taken from `pagination.cursor` of the previous response; omit for the first page.

before.description: Cursor for the previous page, taken from `pagination.cursor` of the previous response. The generated walk only pages forward, with `after`.

response.title: StreamsFrame
response.description: The wire frame: one page of live broadcasts, and the cursor for the next.

data.description: The live broadcasts on this page, most watched first.

id.description: An ID that identifies this broadcast. The video on demand it becomes carries the same id as its `stream_id`.

game_id.description: The ID of the category being streamed; an empty string when the channel has no category set.

game_name.description: The name of the category being streamed; an empty string when the channel has no category set.

type.description: The type of broadcast, `live`. An empty string where Twitch hit an error computing it. Left a bare string on purpose; see the notes.

title.description: The broadcast's title; an empty string if unset.

tags.description: The tags applied to the broadcast.

viewer_count.description: How many people are watching right now.

language.description: The language of the broadcast, as an ISO 639-1 two-letter code, or `other`.

thumbnail_url.description: A URL to a frame from the last five minutes of the broadcast, with a `{width}x{height}` placeholder to replace with the size you want, in pixels.

pagination.description: The cursor for the next page. Twitch sends this object empty once there are no more pages.

unverified.detail: No recording yet: Helix authenticates every call, and the machine this spec was written on holds no Twitch application credentials. The Record workflow fills this in: it reads the application client id and secret from the repository secrets TWITCH_CLIENT_ID and TWITCH_CLIENT_SECRET, mints an app access token through the core, replays this endpoint's `examples/*.request.json` with `truewire capture`, and opens a pull request with the response the API sent.

notes: The response schema is the wire frame, `{"data": [...], "pagination": {...}}`, and no `envelope.payload` is declared, so the method returns the frame and the rows are `result["data"]` (ADR 0010, authoring rule 6). Unwrapping `data` would put the pagination cursor out of reach: pagination paths resolve inside whatever the method returns, and Helix puts the cursor beside `data`, not inside it. One rule for every Helix method is worth more than unwrapping the five endpoints here that never page.

Twitch ends a walk by sending `pagination` as an *empty object*, not by omitting it and not with a null cursor, so the terminator is `absent_cursor` on `pagination.cursor` and a walk stops on the first page whose `pagination` holds no `cursor`.

`type` is left a bare string rather than `enum: ["live"]`: the reference documents one value and then documents an empty string for the error case, which is a second value a `Literal['live']` would reject at runtime.
`tag_ids` and `is_mature` are not declared: the reference marks both deprecated and says they return only an empty array and `false`.

Written from the Helix reference at the `docs` URL above. Fields the reference marks deprecated are not declared; an undeclared field passes validation and is dropped from the validated value, so a recording that carries one is still valid. The first recording confirms or corrects the rest.
